HEADNOTE: Section 16 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rule 3 of the Cenvat Credit Rules, 2004 - Input tax credit -  Period March, 2009 to March, 2015 - Assessee availed cenvat credit on photocopies of invoices - Adjudicating Authority denied cenvat credit - Whether photocopies of invoices were not valid documents for availing cenvat credit - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, assessee could not avail cenvat credit on photocopies of invoices - Held, yes [Para 9.6] [In favour of revenue]GST/Cenvat : Photocopies of invoices are not valid documents for availing cenvat credit and, therefore, assessee cannot avail cenvat credit on photocopies of invoices

FACT: The assessee was engaged in the manufacture of crushing machines and screening machines.

It availed cenvat credit on certain input services.

The Adjudicating Authority denied cenvat credit on input services.

On appeal to Tribunal:

HELD: The Adjudicating Authority has denied cenvat credit alleging that the assessee has not obtained registration as Input Service Distributor (ISD). The assessee has submitted that it has obtained ISD registration in 2008. A copy of the ISD registration is also furnished. Therefore, the disallowance of credit for the reason that the assessee has not obtained ISD registration is unjustified and requires to be set aside. [Paras 9.1 and 9.2]

The Adjudicating Authority has further denied cenvat credit stating that the invoices were raised in the address of Bangalore and Pune office and the credit has been availed in Hosur Unit. The assessee has taken centralized registration incorporating Bangalore and Pune units. In such circumstances, the revenue cannot deny the credit availed on invoices raised in the address of Bangalore and Pune unit. [Para 9.3]

The Adjudicating Authority has also denied cenvat credit on the plea that clearing and forwarding agent services are availed by the assessee outside the factory/place of removal. The definition of input service does not state that the services have to be availed within the factory. The Board Circular No. 999/6/2015-CX, dated 28-1-2015 has also clarified this point. Therefore, the disallowance of credit is unjustified. [Para 9.4]

The assessee has availed credit on debit notes which has been disallowed on plea that these are not valid documents to avail credit. Debit notes can be considered to be valid documents for availing credit when there is no dispute with regard to the service tax paid and the services consumed. In the instant case, the department does not have a contention that the assessee has not discharged the service tax on the said services on which credit has been availed. Therefore, the disallowance of credit on this ground is unjustified. [Para 9.5]

The assessee has availed cenvat credit on photocopies of invoices. The assessee has submitted that the original invoices were misplaced and, therefore, it has availed credit on photocopies. This submission does not find favour. The assessee cannot avail credit on photocopies. These are not valid documents for availing credit. Further if such practice of availing credit on photocopies of invoices is allowed, then it will lead to false claims of credit made by assessees. The claim of assessee on this ground is disallowed. [Para 9.6]

The Adjudicating Authority has disallowed credit on various input services stating that these services are not availed in relation to the activity of manufacture. The assessee has submitted that these services include services like membership charges which are paid for taking membership in industrial association, exhibition stall charges, delegate fee, sales commission, etc. According to assessee, all these services have an integral connection with the manufacture of finished products. These services were consumed to carry out the activity of manufacture effectively and also to provide export of services/goods. The Adjudicating Authority has not made adequate discussion in this regard. The assessee has submitted that it would be able to establish the nexus of the services with the output services/manufacturing activity, if it is given a further chance. Therefore, this issue requires to be remanded to the Adjudicating Authority. [Para 9.7]

In the result, the impugned order is modified to the extent of allowing the credit in respect of the services availed except on photocopies of invoices. The issue with regard to credit disallowed alleging that the services do not have nexus with the manufacturing activity is remanded to the Adjudicating Authority leaving this issue open. [Para 10]

CENVAT Scheme The Cenvat Credit Rules allow credit of duty paid on (i ) capital goods used in the factory of the manufacturer of the final products and (ii) inputs used in or in relation to the manufacture of final products. There are provisions in the Cenvat Credit Rules which deny credit of duty paid on inputs and capital goods if the same are used for manufacturer of exempted final products. The Cenvat scheme enables a manufacturer to take credit of duty paid on the inputs and capital goods and utilize the same for paying duty on excisable goods manufactured by him which are called ‘final products’. If the scheme was to be limited to granting credit only on capital goods and inputs, it would be advantageous for a manufacturer to buy capital goods on payment of duty but it would be disadvantageous if he manufactured the capital goods himself by procuring inputs for the same (such as parts and components) on payment of duty as he would not be able to take credit of duty paid on such inputs because these are not inputs used for manufacturing the final products. It is clear that to obviate such a disadvantageous situation, the scope of ‘input’ has been extended to include goods used in the manufacture of capital goods, which are further used in the factory of the manufacturer. This provision has been made by way of inserting Explanation 2 to the definition of ‘input’ under rule 2(k ), of the Cenvat Credit Rules and, thus, the scheme provides for credit of duty paid on :-

(i)Capital goods used in the factory of the manufacturer of the final products;

(ii)inputs used in or in relation to the manufacture of final products; and

(iii)inputs used in the manufacture of capital goods which are further used in the factory of the manufacturer. [Para 38]

Capital goods

There are other details to the Cenvat scheme and the definition of ‘capital goods’ primarily includes machinery items; components, spares and accessories of the same; and a few other things which have been specifically added such as pollution control equipment; moulds, dies, etc.; refractories; tubes and pipes and fittings thereof; and storage tank. The moulds, dies, refractories, tubes and tank have been specifically added as they would not get classified and included as machinery items, but the rule makers in their wisdom have specifically and additionally included these perhaps considering their functional utility to the manufacturing process. By specifically including these items, credit in respect of duty paid on such items has been allowed which would not otherwise get coverage under the term ‘capital goods’. Secondly, credit of duty paid on inputs used in the manufacture of such specifically listed items has also been allowed. However, factory shed, building foundation and structures (in the manufacture of which the goods, namely, cement and steel items are used) have not been specifically listed under the definition of ‘capital goods’. [Para 39]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Procedure to be observed by manufacturer - Whether gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994, but endorsed after that date, would fall under coverage of Entry No. 10 in Table to Notification No. 16/94-CE (NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently be eligible documents for taking credit under Modvat Scheme - Held, yes [Para 3] Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994, Circular No. 600/37/2001-CX, dated 19-11-2001

FACT: The Tribunal held that the gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994, but endorsed after that date, would fall under the coverage of Entry No. 10 in the Table to the Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently, be eligible documents for taking credit under the Modvat Scheme. It rejected the objection of the revenue that the endorsement should also have been made on the gate-passes on or before 1-4-1994, by observing that endorsed gate-pass was not comparable to the issue of gate-pass because what is mentioned in the proviso to the Notification is that documents should have been issued, which meant that gate-passes should have been issued on or before 1-4-1994.

On reference :

HELD: As per the position prevailing prior to 30-3-1994, when the purchaser resold inputs to third party, he would make an endorsement on the gate pass issued by the manufacturer of the input. Procedure had changed and instead of endorsement on the gate-passes, invoice was required to be produced as per Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994. Certain documents were prescribed for the purpose of giving credit of Modvat under the Rules. In Column No. 3 to the Entry No. 10 of the aforesaid Notification, prescribed documents were endorsed gate-passes/subsidiary gate-passes/certificates. Admittedly, gate-passes were required to be issued by the manufacturer under the procedure then prevailing and as and when the purchaser of the inputs resold inputs to third party, he would make an endorsement on the gate-pass, which would authorise the purchaser to take benefit of the credit of the duties paid on the goods. From the language of the said Notification, it is clear that benefit could be given if the documents would have been issued before 1-4-1994 and credit had been taken on or before 30-6-1994. From this, it was clear that gate-passes could be issued before 1-4-1994 and the benefit of credit could be taken on or before 30-6-1994. Transaction of sale or re-sale could take place any time prior to 30th June and on endorsement of same being made, benefit could be taken on or before 30-6-1994. The language of the Notification nowhere requires that the endorsement should also be made before 1-4-1994. [Para 1]

Therefore, gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994 but endorsed after that date would fall under the coverage of Entry No. 10 in the Table to the Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently, be eligible documents for taking credit under the Modvat Scheme. [Para 3]

Accordingly, I set aside this part of the order and allow the appeal to that extent. 4. The second point requiring consideration of the Tribunal is whether modvat credit can be disallowed on the ground when the invoice is in the name of the branch office of the appellant whereas the inputs were received in the factory premises of the appellants and were utilised therein. The department's objection is that as per the Trade Notice No. 18/95 dated 21.2.1995 issued by the Allahabad Collectorate goods covered under a particular invoice should be delivered only at the place of destination reflected in the said invoice and in the instant case the goods have been delivered in the factory premises of the appellant whereas the address shown in the invoice is that of their branch office. I find that the same issue had come up earlier before the Tribunal in the case of Larsen & Toubro, Orissa Vs. Collector of Central Excise, Bhubaneswar reported in 1994 (3) RLT 215 (ERB) wherein it was held that modvat credit should not be on the ground that the duty paying documents were in the name of the office whereas the inputs were received and utilised in the factory. In the instant case, there is no dispute that the invoice is in the name of the same appellant. Further, the department also does not dispute the duty-paid character of the inputs, their receipt in the appellants' factory and its utilisation in the manufacture of final product or the clearance of the final product on payment of duty. In nutshell, the availability of the modvat credit to the appellant on all other counts is not denied by the department. The appellants' reliance on Board's Circular No. 96/7/95-CX dated 13.2.1995 which is to the effect that in case of transit sale, invoices which may be in the assessees registered office can be endorsed by them in the name of their factory premises, is appropriate. In the instant case, the documents were in the name of branch office. The branch office could have endorsed the same in their own factory address. In the circumstances, it is only a procedural lapse, if at all, on the part of the appellants and cannot be made the basis for denial of modvat credit to the appellants. Accordingly, I allow this part of the appeal also by setting aside the order of the lower authority to that extent.

5. As regards the denial of modvat credit on the ground that dealers invoices are defective in character, I find that the original adjudicating authority in his impugned order has himself observed that as the goods were sold to the appellants as 'transit sale', the manufacturer's invoices bearing end-user's name would have been sufficient and proper documents to enable the appellant to take the credit. However, after observing so, he goes further to the dealers invoices and refers some defects in the said invoices and by holding the dealers invoices as defective disallowed the modvat credit. I find sufficient force in the submission of Shri Dutta that having himself observed that manufacturer's invoices were sufficient to extend the benefit of modvat credit to the appellants, the Assistant Collector has erred in relying on dealers invoices and rejecting the appellants claim for modvat by holding the same to be improper documents. I find that the Assistant Collector should have looked into the manufacturer's invoices and should have allowed the benefit of modvat after satisfying himself about the correctness of the same. As the manufacturer's invoices have not been looked into by the Assistant Collector from that angle, I set aside the impugned order and remand the case to the original adjudicating authority with the directions to verify the particulars required to be mentioned in the manufacturer's invoices under the law and to extend the benefit, if available, on the basis of the manufacturer's invoices.

6. In view of the foregoing discussions, penalty of Rs. 5,000/- is also set aside.

7. Appeal disposed of in the above terms.

Per Gowri Shankar : The question for consideration in this appeal is the eligibility to modvat credit by the appellant of the duty that is shown to have been paid on the invoices issued by the dealers of the inputs. After hearing both sides, we deal with each of the grounds on which modvat has been denied, as follows:-

2. A sum of Rs. 2.21 lakhs had been denied on the ground that the invoice bore the address of the appellant's head office and not that of the factory. Counsel for the appellant says that there was only one manufacturing unit located at Pune, the head office being in Mumbai. The head office could not have taken the credit, not being a factory. Endorsement of invoices is also not permissible. The goods had been received in the appellant's factory and utilised in the manufacture. Therefore the failure, if any, is most technical and should not stand in the way. The departmental representative emphasises that the invoice is not in the name of the manufacturing unit.

3. In a situation of this kind where there is only one factory, we are of the view that the drawback in the invoice that it did not contain the factory's name, should not result in the invoice being held invalid. The head office was not a factory and so could not have utilised the credit. The provisions of Rule 57F (1), permitting removal of the inputs for home consumption as such, would also not be available to it. It is not as if, by containing the heading office's name, credit could have been taken by the recipient in more than one factory; as we have noted, the factory was only one. There is no dispute that the goods were not received and utilised in the factory. In this situation, we do not think that the credit should be denied.

4. Invoices issued by dealers for a total of Rs. 7.49 lakhs have been held invalid on the ground that they were not marked duplicate or original and they were "extra copies". The invoices were issued between the period from 3rd August 1994 to 4th January 1995. The contention of the counsel for the appellant is that the requirement that credit must be been taken on duplicate invoices came on the statute book by way of amendment of sub-rule (4) of Rule 57GG on 19.1.1995. The trade notice that was issued in November 1994 by the Commissioner, Pune, insisting upon this requirement had no legal authority.

5. Although the departmental representative relies on the trade notice, the appellant's contention has to be accepted. In the absence of any legal authority, the denial of the credit is not justified. This is the view taken by the Tribunal in its decisions in Lauls Ltd. Vs. CCE 2000 (41) RLT 213 and Parikh Chemical Industries Vs. CCE 1997 (95) ELT 598. Another objection raised with regard to these invoices is that they did not contain details of the mode of transport and time. The Commissioner has confirmed that these invoices did not indicate the mode and time of transport. Counsel for the appellant points out, rightly, that the proforma prescribed under sub-rule (4) of Rule 57GG did not contain time and mode of transport. Column 1 (i) of the proforma specifies "date and time of issue both in words and figures of the invoice of registered person issuing the invoice." This refers to the date of issue of the invoice and not the date and time of despatch of the goods from the premises. The contention of the departmental representative that some of the invoices did not contain this also may be true; that however was not the basis for proposing to disallow these invoices. The basis was very clear that time and mode of transport had not been shown. We therefore do not think that this was a valid objection and credit ought not to have been denied.

6. The credit of 36000/- has been objected to on the ground that it was a customer copy of an invoice issued by Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL for short) and not a duplicate. We do not see how reliance made on a Circular 86/86/94-CX dated 22.12.1994 of the Board helps the appellant. This only provides that SAIL can issue invoices from the depot recognised for modvat credit purposes and has anything to do with any copy. There being no other ground, the denial of the credit is in order.

7. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.

Per Gowri Shankar :

The notice issued to the respondent to these appeals proposed denial of modvat credit on the ground that it had been taken on invoices which was issued to the assessee's head office, and had been endorsed by it from that head office to its factory at Sion. The Assistant Collector confirmed the proposal in the notice and held that credit was not available. On appeal by the assessee from this order, the Commissioner (Appeals) noted that the head office could not avail modvat credit, not having the manufacturing facility. It also could not endorse the gate passes to its own factory, not being a dealer. Hence the very purpose of modvat credit will be denied. He therefore held that it could not be denied. This is appealed by the department.

2. The ground in the department's appeal is the same as was in the show cause notice, that the invoices were addressed, not to factory but to head office of the assessee and the assessee could not endorse these documents to its own factory.

3. I agree that it is meaningless for an assessee to endorse documents to itself. Endorsement of a document is resorted to signify that title to the goods mentioned in that document is passed on. There can be no question of one person passing the title to another person. Endorsement on these invoices therefore has no legal significance.

4. Representative of the respondent cites before me the decision of the Tribunal in Larsen Toubro Ltd. Vs. CCE 1994 (3) RLT 215 (CEGAT)=1994 (72) ELT 948. The question for decision by the Tribunal was whether credit should be taken by Larsen Toubro and the duty shown to have been paid on the bill of entry, which showed as the importer's address at the company's head office. The credit was actually taken by factory elsewhere. The Tribunal noted that the import of the goods was dealt with by the head office and it was natural that the head office should figure on the bill of entry.

5. In my view, the same consideration would apply to the facts before me. The representative of the respondents explains that the purchase of the goods for use in the two factories of the respondent, then situated at Sion and Mankhurd was processed at the head office at Tardeo and the goods therefore first came to the head office and were thereafter sent to the factory. In a case where the invoices are addressed to the head office, which cannot utilise the credit that office merely passes the goods on to the factory, for being utilised there, I do not see there is any contravention of the rules. In these circumstances, I do not find any ground for interference.

6. Appeal dismissed.

Per Justice Shri U.L. Bhat, President :

Appellant, M/s. Heinz India Pvt. Ltd., Bombay with Head Office at Bombay has a factory in Aligarh for manufacture of Complan and other nutrients. Appellant was availing Modvat credit on certain inputs. The dispute arose on scrutiny of monthly RT 12 Return for October 94. Various items of Modvat were objected to. After hearing the appellant, the objection regarding Rs. 53,309 being the duty element of the input covered by Invoice Nos. 1062, 1075 and 1081 issued by the manufacturer was confirmed and corresponding amount of duty demanded, though other objections were dropped. Confirmation of the demand by the Assistant Commissioner having been confirmed by the Commissioner (Appeals), the present appeal has been filed.

2. Copies of three invoices in question are before me. They were issued by the manufacturer of inputs to M/s. Heinz India Pvt. Ltd. Bombay. In the column against destination, Aligarh is seen mentioned. The case of the appellant that order for the input was placed by the Head Office at Bombay for use at the factory in Aligarh is not denied by the Department. The lower authorities objected to the admissibility of Modvat credit on the ground that the invoices were endorsed by the Head Office in favour of factory. Being governed by the Central Excise Rules, 1944, central excise licence was taken in respect of the Aligarh factory in the name of Heinz India Pvt. Ltd. Aligarh. This does not mean that there are two different companies called M/s. Heinz India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Heinz India Pvt. Ltd. Aligarh. There is only one entity M/s. Heinz India Pvt. Ltd. Bombay with head office at Bombay and this company has factory at several places including the factory at Aligarh. It is evident from the invoices that order was placed by the Head Office at Bombay for supply to and use in the Aligarh unit. That being so, it cannot be said that there is endorsement on the invoices by one entity to another. The expression "endorsement" has been used only loosely in this context. This is not a case of transfer of inputs by one legal entity to a third party. This is a case where supply had been arranged by Head Office for the use of the factory.

There can be no legal objection to the availment of Modvat credit on the basis of invoices issued in the name of the company at its registered Head Office, though used in the factory at Aligarh. This view is supported by the decisions of the Tribunal in the cases of Larsen Toubro Ltd. 1994 (72) ELT 948 (T), Bansal Containers (P) Ltd. 1994 (3) RLT 215(CEGAT) = 1996 (83) ELT 425 (T), Siyaram Platex (P) Ltd. 1994 (73) ELT 915 (T) and Snow Cem India Ltd. 1994 (4) RLT 119 (CEGAT) = 1997 (96) ELT 627 (T).

3. In this view, the appellant was entitled to avail Modvat credit on the basis of the invoices referred to above.

4. The impugned orders are set aside and the appeal is allowed.

Per G.R. Sharma :

This is an appeal against the findings of the Ld. Commissioner (Appeals). In impugned order dt. 27.11.98. Ld. Commissioner (Appeals) in this order had held

"I have considered the submissions. I find that the appellants case of transfer of goods from one manufacturing unit to another is not covered by the Board's Circular allowing credit for endorsement made on documents addressed to head office. The appellants' submission that the unit endorsing documents may be considered as 'Head office' has no basis. Head Office registered offices are declared places as such and there is no point to consider a place as Head Office or Registered Office. The appellants' case is not covered by the case law cited by them. The appellants have failed to give any corporative evidence to show the actual use of the items; movement of goods were in original packing accompanying documents and as to how the documents were endorsed by the midway factory without the goods even entering the unit as submitted by them. I uphold the impugned order. The appeal is rejected".

2. The facts of the case briefly stated are that the appellants are engaged in the manufacture of loudspeakers. They are availing Modvat credit. During the course of scrutiny of their records, Revenue authorities noticed that the assessee had taken Modvat credit amounting to Rs. 2,98,661/- against documents which were not found to have been issued in their address. The Department alleged that those were not valid documents under Rule 57G. The Bills of Entry in the instant case were issued in the name of another manufacturing unit M/s. Salora International Ltd., Noida, Sector 16. These Bills of Entries were later on endorsed in the name of M/s. Salora International Ltd., Phase II, Noida. Accordingly, a SCN was issued to the appellants asking them to explain as to why the Modvat credit should not be denied to them.

3. The Asstt. Commissioner adjudicated the case on 27.11.97 disallowing Modvat credit and also ordering payment of interest. When the appellants filed an appeal. Ld. Commissioner (Appeals) held as indicated above.

4. Arguing the case for the appellants Shri M.A. Rangaswamy, Ld. Counsel submits that M/s. Salora International Ltd. have two units at Noida; that Bills of Entry were in the name of one unit which endorsed them to the other unit. He submits that the goods alongwith the endorsed Bill of Entry were received in the second unit and the second unit took Modvat credit. He referred to Board's Circular No. 179/13/96-CX dt. 29.2.96 [reported in 1996 (13) RLT M44] stating that by this circular, the Board clarified in para 3

"3. It has been decided that credit should not be denied where the Bill of Entry is in the name of the Registered Office/Head Office provided that

(a)

the entire consignment covered by the said Bill of Entry is received in the factory in original packed conditions

(b)

triplicate copy of Bill of Entry/duplicate copy of Bill of entry generated on EDI system is endorsed by the Registered Office/Head Office to the effect that consignment covered by the Bill of entry are delivered to the manufacturing unit for availing credit".

Ld. Counsel submits that the above circular of the Board was modified partly by Circular No. 211/45/96-CX. dt. 14.5.96 [reported in 1996 (14) RLT M83]. Ld. Counsel also referred to Board's Circular No. 207/41/96-CX. dt. 1.5.96 [reported in 1996 (14) RLT M48].

5. Ld. Counsel further submitted that the Central Board of Excise & Customs by his Circular No. 275/109/96-CX. dt. 26.11.96 [reported in 1996 (17) RLT M71] examined a point reading as

"A request has been made to provide a procedure when the inputs are imported in the name of manufacturer who instead of availing the credit, transfer such inputs to his sister unit".

It was clarified in that Trade Notice as

The procedure prescribed by the Board under Circular No. 179/13/96-CX dt. 29.2.96 in case of the Bill of Entry in the name of Registered Office/Head Office can be followed mutatis-mutandis in these cases also".

Ld. Counsel submits that having regard to the above clarifications given by the Board, their case is squarely covered by the above Circular of the Board which is reported in 1996 (88) ELT.T.58.

Briefly stated the facts of the case are as follows:-

1.1. The respondents herein availed MODVAT Credit of Rs. 1,01,009.00 during the period from 17.2.93 to 8.3.93 in respect of an input namely Formaldehyde received by them from a Public Sector Unit, M/s. Hindustan Organic Chemicals Ltd. (HOCL). The Gate Passes issued by the HOCL as an evidence of payment of duty on the said consignment of Formaldehyde, were in the name of the respondent company, M/s. Mangalam Timber Products Ltd. on their Head Office at Calcutta. It was, therefore, found after issue of the show cause notice by the Original Authority that the goods received by the Head Office at Calcutta, were sold inasmuch as the Gate Passes did not carry any endorsement of the Calcutta Head Office in the name of the respondents' factory premises at Kusumi, Nawarangpur, Bhubaneswar Commissionerate of Central Excise.

1.2 On this basis, the Assistant Commissioner concerned disallowed the MODVAT Credit of Rs. 1,01,009.00. He also imposed a personal penalty of Rs. 1,000.00.

1.3. On appeal before the lower appellate authority, the respondents herein succeeded. The said Appellate Authority has observed as follows:-

".....The point of dispute is whether the non-endorsement of the gate passes in favour of the appellant's factory would be sufficient to deny credit. Here the most important feature is that the appellants have duty paying documents which are in favour or their Head Office. Inadvertently, those were not endorsed in favour of the appellant's factory. I find that the defect mentioned in the Show Cause Notice is a remedial defect. The technical requirement cannot come in the way in the availment of substantive benefit of the MODVAT Credit. Regarding the allegation of fraudulent availment of MODVAT Credit. I find that the same is baseless. The allegation is based on mere presumption. The department did not take any action to ascertain or to investigate as to whether inputs covering the gate passes had been received at the factory or not. In fact, the Assistant Collector has failed to establish his contention with substantive evidence."

Hence this appeal by the Revenue.

2. Learned J.D.R., Shri S.N. Ghosh for the appellant Commissioner now submits that non-endorsement of the gate passes by the respondents' Calcutta Head Office to their factory at Nawarangpur is only one of the issues in the Adjudication Order passed by the Assistant Commissioner. The other point was that the goods had been sold by the Calcutta Head Office. In the absence of any evidence to the contrary adduced by the respondents herein that they had actually received the goods in respect of these Gate Passes issued by HOCL. He, therefore, submits that the Order of the lower Appellate Authority is not correct on facts when he observes that' as regards the allegation of fraudulent availment of MODVAT Credit, the same is based on mere presumption.' He, further, points out that the lower Appellate Authority's observation that the Department ought to have taken some action to ascertain or to investigate as to whether the inputs covering the Gate Passes had been received at the factory or not, was not called for inasmuch as it was the onus of the respondents to prove that they had received the goods in respect of the concerned Gate Passes and therefore, the MODVAT Credit was rightly taken and that it was merely a clerical error on the part of HOCL to show the 'Consignee' as Calcutta Office.

3. Opposing the contentions, learned Advocate, Shri S.K. Bagaria on the other hand, submits that before the lower Appellate Authority all the evidences to the effect that the goods had been received by the respondents from HOCL directly at the factory premises at Nawarangpur, was produced before the lower Appellate Authority. When the said Authority makes an observation that the allegation of fraudulent availment of MODVAT Credit is baseless and without any evidence, it is presumed that he must have gone by the evidence placed by the respondents before the said Authority, since the evidence was annexed to the appeal before it.

4. As regards the question that the Calcutta Office should have endorsed the Gate Passes in the name of the factory, he submits that this issue is no longer res integra in view of the Tribunal's Judgement in the case of Larsen & Toubro vs. Collector of Central Excise reported in 1994 (72) ELT-948 = 1994 (3) RLT 215 (CEGAT-ERB) (relevant para : First Head Note). Even the subsequent Reference Application on that question has also been rejected.

entries made for the same cannot be accepted as reflecting the actual position. As regards the Board's circular he submits that it is admitted fact that their invoice in question has not been endorsed by their head office in [sic] their factory and as such the conditions of the circular are not satisfied. If the goods were transported by a taxi they could have mentioned the taxi number etc. in the invoice itself. In the circumstances he submits that there is no case made up for grant of stay to the applicants. 4. I have considered the submissions made from both the sides. The dispute is limited to only one invoice in question. The Modvat credit has been disallowed by not accepting the said invoice on the ground that the same shows the address of their head office instead of the factory and there is no endorsement by the head office. Further the department has also doubted the actual receipt of the goods in their factory premises because the applicants have failed to produce any documents showing the actual receipt and [since] the transporters' column in the invoices [having been]left blank. However, I find that the applicants have explained before the Assistant Commissioner, vide their reply to the show cause notice, that the input in question was transported personally by one of their employees in asmuchas the same was only 115.3 K.gs. of stainless steel wire for which a regular transport was not required. They had also produced the good's receipt report. I have seen the photocopy of the report produced on record. The same is carrying a printed serial number and is duly signed by their store-keeper. I also find that the cardex maintained by them reflects the receipt of the above material. Further, there is no dispute or doubt about the fact that the said material was duly entered in their RG-23A Part-I record. Having entered the goods in their Modvatable raw material register, the applicants could not have escaped to show the utilisation of the same in the manufacture of final product and to clear the final product on payment of duty. It is not a case where the applicants have availed the Modvat credit in their Part-II register without the corresponding receipt of raw material in their part I register. As such I find that the failure on the part of the applicants to show the transporters' mode in the invoice, to take the goods first to their head office, got the invoice endorsed in their factory and then transport the goods to their factory are no reasons for denial of benefit of Modvat credit to them. Endorsement of the invoice by their own head office is a rectifiable defect in any case. Taking all these issues into consideration I hold that the applicants had made out a prima facie case for granting them unconditional stay. I Order accordingly.

5. As only above points are involved in the appeal, I take up the appeal itself and allow the same. The impugned order is set aside.

More so, when an invoice issued in the name of the customer an invoice cannot be endorsed thus, the pre-authentication of an invoice is a curable defect more so when it is issued not by the customer (who takes modvat credit) but by the supplier. Therefore, if there is a defect, the defect should be rectified only by the supplier. We therefore, hold that pre-authentication is a curable defect and can be rectified. 16. In so far as Credit of duty on original invoices is concerned, it was submitted by the appellants that a request was made stating that the original invoice was lost, but this request was not considered by the concerned authorities in view of the fact that a show cause notice was already issued. We find that different Benches of this Tribunal have held that during the initial period of introduction of invoice system, MODVAT Credit could be taken on the strength of original invoice. No doubt a case was cited by the Revenue in support of their contention that it was only in cases of loss of the duplicate invoices in transit that MODVAT Credit could be on the strength of original copy of the invoice. However, the case cited by the Revenue pertained to loss of invoice in the factory. In view of the consistent view held by the Tribunal that MODVAT Credit could be taken on the strength of original invoice during the initial period of introduction of MODVAT Credit scheme on the strength of invoice we do not find any reasons to disagree with the contention of the appellant and hold accordingly.

17. 18. In so far as disallowance of MODVAT Credit amounting to Rs. 29,346/- on the ground that the document does not meet the requirements of Rule 52A is concerned, we find that the delivery note clearly makes a mention about payment of duty as per enclosure and we find that the particulars given in the enclosure are in accordance with requirement of Rule 52A. We therefore, hold that MODVAT Credit has correctly been taken in this respect.

19. The only issue now remains is that of taking Credit on the strength of invoices in which the address of the Head Office of the Company was given. In this case, we note that there is no dispute about the actual receipt of the goods in the factory and their utilisation thereof. Therefore, the fact that the address recorded in the invoice was that of Head Office of the appellants' unit does not debar them from taking MODVAT Credit on the strength of this type of documents. Therefore, MODVAT Credit will be admissible to them in this respect.

20. In so far as imposition of penalty is concerned, we note that a part of the credit has been reversed. Looking to all the facts and circumstance discussed above, we hold that penalty is imposable, but the quantum of penalty is too high. Looking to the totality of the circumstances, we reduce the quantum of penalty to Rs. 25,000/-.

Commissioner of Customs & Central Excise (Appeals).

Bangalore has erred in allowing Modvat Credit on the strength of endorsed invoices.

ii)

Commissioner of Customs & Central Excise (Appeals),

Bangalore has failed to appreciate that endorsed invoices are not the documents prescribed by the Central Board of Excise & Customs for the purpose of availment of Mod vat Credit. Hence the assessee is not entitled to take Modvat Credit on endorsed invoices.

"On a careful consideration of the record of the case and the submission of the appellants, I find that it is a fact that the Board's circular No. 53/86C8.6 dated 5.12.86 permits in respect of proforma credit, endorsement of G.Ps by the first consignee to another if he purchases the entire consignment in original packed condition subsequently, Board's circular No. 14/89 dated 17.4.89 permitted the second endorsement also. The West Regional Bench in the case of SBS Organics Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Collector of Central Excise & Customs dealing with a similar issue and also the Trade Notice No. 86/89 dated 12.5.89 of Baroda Collectorate has observed as under:-

" The main issue to be decided in this appeal is whether the denial of modvat credit in respect of inputs received under gate passes endorsed in favour of the appellants after passing through more than two hands, is sustainable. Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules stipulates that inputs are to be received under the cover of a gate pass, an AR-I, a Bill of Entry or any other document as may be prescribed by the Board. Gate pass is a document prescribed for removal of the goods from the factory of manufacturer to the first destination. This is evident from the provisions of Rule 52A and Rule 173G of the Central Excise Rules. Hence, when there is a stipulation in Rule 57G that the inputs are to be received under gate pass by the claimant of modvat credit, it should be normally taken to mean that the said Rule contemplates receipt of inputs straight from the factory of manufacturer under gate pass. In that case, the consignee is necessarily to be the modvat claimant and consignor being the manufacturer of inputs, However, when this requirement created some difficulties in the case of Small Scale Units to obtain the inputs through intermediaries the Board appears to have made relaxation to this requirement, by permitting one endorsement in the gate passes initially and subsequently based on the representations permitting up to two endorsements in the gate passes. This relaxation made by the Board appears to be purely of administrative nature based on consideration of implementing the modvat scheme, so long as the duty paid nature of the goods and duty paid thereon could be established. As seen from the Trade Notice cited by the learned Advocate, it is evident that the Government is keen to extend the modvat credit so long as the goods in factory packed condition as are covered by the gate passes are received by the parties intending to avail modvat credit. Going by this spirit of the relaxation, we are unable appreciate the routine and mechanical approach of the authorities below in rejecting the claim of the modvat credit only on the ground that more than one endorsement have been made. When the Board themselves have taken a decision to relax the procedural requirement by way of administrative instruction it should be the endeavour of the authorities to extend modvat credit wherever, the duty paid nature of the goods is evident from the gate passes produced and quantum of duty paid on the inputs could be ascertained from them. A positive approach is called for in this regard. We also take note of the argument of Shri Arya that permitting a number of endorsements would involve in considerable administrative burden and the gate passes are likely to be abused. In this case, it is contended by the other side that the previous endorsements have been made not by any other manufacturer who could utilise this inputs but only by intermediaries in the trade channel. In any case, the department is entitled to make verification or investigation with regard to the genuineness of the gate pass and also the question whether gate pass has been utilised for availment of modvat credit at the earliest stages. In this case, no such enquiry appears to have been conducted and the modvat credit has been denied only on the ground that more than that of permitted endorsements have been made in the gate passes. Such an order cannot be sustainable in the context of the scheme of modvat credit read along with the relaxation made by the Board."

As regards the other invoices, it is seen that though the address on the invoices is that of their Kim factory, the said invoices mentioned that the inputs are to be delivered at the Surat factory. In these circumstances, the Tribunal's decision in the case of Larsen Toubro Ltd. holding that when the invoices have been issued in the name of the office but the goods are received in the factory, the same would constitute proper modvatable documents, have to be applied. As regards the modvat credit taken on the basis of certificates issued by the Superintendent prior to 31.3.1994, it is seen that the notification itself provides for taking credit on the basis of such documents provided the credit is taken before 30.6.1994. As such, we do not find any lapse on the part of the appellant to avail the credit on the basis of the said documents especially when there is no doubt or dispute about the receipt of the inputs by the appellants in their factory, their utilisation in the manufacture of the final product and clearance of the final product on payment of duty.

CCE 2000 (40) RLT 575 (CEGAT-LB)=RLT (L.B.-CEGAT)-1907=2000 (121) ELT 247 wherein the Tribunal, after taking note of the Board's circular, has observed that the minor procedural lapses, if any, should not be made the basis for denial of the benefit of the modvat credit, if the assessee's jurisdictional Assistant Commissioner is otherwise satisfied about the receipt of the inputs. In the absence of any doubt to the above fact, we are of the view that the impugned orders are liable to be set aside.

ANNEX 12.2

[PARA 12.2-3]

CIRCULAR NO. 179/13/96-CX, DATED 29-2-1996

PROBLEMS FACED IN AVAILING MODVAT ON BILL OF ENTRY IN THE NAME OF REGISTERED OFFICE/HEAD OFFICE BUT CREDIT TO BE AVAILED BY THE FACTORY

Attention of the Board has been invited to the difficulties faced by the manufacturers in availing the credit under rule 57G/57T where :

(i)

the Bill of Entry has been filed in the name of the registered office/head office of the manufacturer for the inputs to be used in his factory.

(ii)

imported goods lying in customs dock area/bonded warehouse are diverted to manufacturing units in whose name Bill of Entry has not been filed.

(iii)

domestic duty paid goods consigned to a manufacturing unit are diverted in whole or part from a duty paid godown of the manufacturer or such diversion is affected in transit.

2. The issue has been examined by the Board.

3. It has been decided that credit should not be denied where the Bill of Entry is in the name of the registered office/head office provided that :—

(a)

the entire consignment covered by the said Bill of Entry is received in the factory in original packed conditions.

(b)

triplicate copy of Bill of Entry/duplicate copy of the Bill of Entry generated on EDI system is endorsed by the registered office/head office to the effect that consignment covered by the Bill of Entry are delivered to the manufacturing unit for availing credit.

4. Where the imported goods are still in Customs dock area and the manufacturer- importer decides to divert/transfer the goods, a declaration by the manufacturer- importer can be made on the reverse of triplicate copy of Bill of Entry/duplicate copy of the Bill of Entry generated on EDI system by the manufacturer-importer that consignments are being delivered to the unit (name of the unit) for availing credit and endorsed by the proper Officer of Customs for enabling the manufacturing unit to avail credit.

5. In cases where the imported goods are lying in the bonded warehouse from where diversion takes place either of entire consignment or part consignment, credit can be permitted provided ex-bond Bill of Entry is filed for such entire/part consignments and that a declaration is made on the reverse of the said ex-bond triplicate copy of the Bill of Entry/duplicate copy of the Bill of Entry generated on EDI system to the effect that consignments are delivered to a unit (name of the unit) for availing credit.

6. In all cases duty-paying documents on the basis of which credit has been availed in aforesaid cases, should be submitted to the Range Superintendent for the necessary verification and defacing/endorsement.

7. In case of split consignments and other types of cases not covered by the preceding paragraphs the inputs can be cleared on the payment of duty as envisaged under rule 57F/57S and on the basis of such duty-paying documents credit can be availed.

2. From the record, I find that the appellants have a strong, prima facie, case as the modvat credit has been disallowed to them of the disputed amount on technical ground. Therefore, the stay application is allowed.

3. With the consent of both sides, I proceed to decide the appeal itself on merits.

4. This appeal has been filed by the appellants against a part of the impugned order-in-appeal dated 8.5.2002 vide which the Commissioner (Appeals) has disallowed the modvat credit of Rs. 8,36,297.

5. The appellants are engaged in the manufacture of steel tubes and pipes. They during the period March 1998 to June 1999 availed the modvat credit of Rs. 8,36,297/- on the invoices/B.Es, but they were served with a show cause notice for recovery of this amount on the ground that the invoices/B.Es did not contain their name and address and there were also no endorsements on those documents in their favour. After getting their reply to the show cause notice, the adjudicating authority confirmed the demand through the order-in-original. On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) has also upheld that order through the impugned order.

6. I have heard both sides.

7. The learned counsel has contended that there is no cogent evidence to substantiate the allegations as alleged in the show cause notice against the appellants. He has also referred to the letter issued by the SAIL from whom the goods were purchased in respect of which the modvat credit has been claimed, clarifying all the objections raised by the Department in the show cause notice. But the same, according to the learned counsel, has been overlooked by the Commissioner (Appeals). Therefore, the impugned order of the Commissioner (Appeals) disallowing the modvat credit of the disputed amount deserves to be set aside.

8. On the other hand, the learned SDR, has simply reiterated the correctness of the impugned order. The perusal of the record shows that the modvat credit of the disputed amount has been taken by the appellants on the strength of 15 invoices and one Bill of Entry. The invoices were issued by the registered dealer i.e. SAIL. On the invoices, initially the factory address of the appellants was not mentioned, but address of the Head Office was recorded therein. But, later on, this position was clarified by the SAIL through letter (refer page 41) dated 18.12.1998 and address on the invoices was corrected. There is no dispute regarding the duty paid character of the goods as they were sold to the appellants by the SAIL. There is no evidence to suggest that the goods were not delivered at the factory premises by the SAIL. The observations of the Commissioner (Appeals) in para 13 of the impugned order that there was no endorsement in favour of the factory by the Head/Regd. Offices of the appellants and that there was no balance in the quantity of the raw materials issued vis-a-vis final product/waste/burning losses, while disallowing the modvat credit claimed by the appellants, had been based on no evidence whatsoever. No endorsement of the Head Office was required when the address on the invoices itself was corrected by the SAIL, the supplier of the goods, through letter dated 18.12.1998, referred to above. No material has been brought on record to show that there was no balance in the quantity of the raw-materials issued vis-a-vis final product. When the duty paid character of the goods stands amply established and there had been also receipt of the goods in the factory, the modvat credit claimed, could not be legally denied to the appellants. In this context, reference may be made to Aradhana Beverages Food Co. Ltd. Vs. CCE, Bolpur, 1999 (35) RLT 152, wherein in similar circumstances, this view has been taken by the Tribunal.

9. In the light of the discussion made above, the impugned order of the Commissioner (Appeals) disallowing the modvat credit of disputed amount of Rs. 8,36,297/- to the appellants, cannot be sustained and the same is ordered to be set aside. The appeal of the appellants is accordingly allowed with consequential relief, if any, permissible under the law.

HEADNOTE: Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Gate pass endorsements--procedure cannot deny Mod vat so long as duty has been paid on the inputs. Three endorsements on original gate pass accepted

FACT: The appellants had taken Modvat credit for goods received against GP J, after it had been endorsed three times by different parties and a demand for Rs. 1,02,600.00 was confirmed. Their appeal was also rejected by the Collector (Appeals).

HELD: Modvat--cannot be denied in routine or by mechanical approach even if documentation is defective so long as duty has been paid on inputs, "... we are unable to appreciate the routine and mechanical approach of the authorities below in rejecting the claim of the Modvat credit only on the ground that more than one endorsement has been made. When the Board themselves have taken a decision to relax the procedural requirement by way of administrative instruction it should be the endeavour of the authorities to extend Modvat credit wherever the duty-paid nature of the goods is evident from the gate passes produced and quantum of duty paid on the inputs could be ascertained from them. A positive approach is called for in this regard."

2. Modvat--credit for goods received against GP I, after three endorsements by different parties can be allowed as long as duty-paid nature of the goods is established. "Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules stipulates that inputs are to be received under the cover of a gate pass, an AR-I, a Bill of Entry or any other document as may be prescribed by the Board. ...However, when this requirement created some difficulties in the ease of Small Scale units to obtain the inputs through intermediaries, the Board appears to have made relaxation to this requirement by permitting one endorsement in the gate pass initially and subsequently based on the representations permitting upto two endorsements in the gate passes. This relaxation made by the Board appears to be purely of administrative nature based on considerations of implementing the Modvat scheme, so long as the duty-paid nature of the goods and duty paid thereon could be established. As seen from the Trade Notice cited by the learned advocate, it is evident that the Government is keen to extend the Modvat credit so long as the goods in factory packed condition as are covered by the gate passes are received by the parties intending to avail Modvat credit...... the department is entitled to make verification or investigation with regard to the genuineness of the gate pass and also on the question whether gate pass has been utilised for availment of Modvat credit at the earliest stages. In this case, no such enquiry appears to have been conducted and the Modvat credit has-been denied only on the ground that more than that of permitted endorsements have been made in the gate passes. Such an order cannot be sustainable in the context of the scheme of Modvat credit read along with the relaxation made by the Board. We, therefore, set aside the order passed by the authorities below and permit availment of credit and while doing so, we allow the liberty to the Assistant Collector to cause any inquiry or investigation to satisfy himself about the genuine nature of the gate passes and also about non-utilisation of the gate passes at the earlier stages of endorsements for availment of Modvat credit."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Procedure to be observed by manufacturer- ‘E’ Ltd. imported a consignment of shredded steel which was cleared under bill of entry on payment of countervailing duty - A portion of said goods imported was given as loan to appellant - Appellant availed credit of duty on goods received from ‘E’ Ltd. - Revenue denied credit of duty to appellant on ground that bill of entry was not endorsed in its name - However, Superintendent of Central Excise issued certificate that ‘E’ Ltd. had not taken credit of duty paid on goods which were given as loan to appellant and goods received by appellant were used in its factory as input - Whether since rule 57G does not require that for taking credit of duty, bill of entry should be endorsed in name of claimant, credit of duty could not be denied on that ground to appellant - Held, yes - Whether, further, since bill of entry together with certificate issued by authority clearly showed that goods imported and cleared under bills of entry on payment of duty, were received and utilized by appellant as inputs in its factory and that assessee had not utilized credit of duty paid on said goods, authorities below were not justified in denying credit of duty to appellant - Held, yes

FACT: E Ltd. had imported a consignment of shredded scrap and cleared the same on payment of duty. Out of the said consignment, ‘E’ Ltd. gave certain quantity of shredded scrap to the appellant as a loan. On receipt of said goods, the appellant took credit of duty of the amount equivalent to customs duty paid by ‘E’ Ltd. on those goods. However, the revenue denied credit of duty to the appellant on the ground that it had taken credit of duty on basis of delivery challans issued by ‘E’ Ltd. but credit of duty could not be taken under rule 57G on that basis. On adjudication, the Commissioner confirmed the demand of duty on the appellant along with penalty. On appeal, the Tribunal also confirmed the demand on the ground that bills of entry were not endorsed in the name of the appellant.

On appeal :

HELD: Rule 57G clearly shows that the credit of duty can be taken on inputs by establishing that the duty has been paid on the said inputs on the basis of documents such as invoice, AR-1, Bill on Entry, etc. In the instant case, it was not in dispute that the appellant had received imported shredded steel scrap from ‘E’ Ltd. on which countervailing duty had been paid by ‘E’ Ltd. It was also not in dispute that ‘E’ Ltd. had not taken credit of the duty paid on shredded steel scrap which was given on loan to the appellant. It was also not in dispute that the appellant had used the said shredded steel scrap taken on loan from ‘E’ Ltd. as inputs in its factory. The certificate issued by a Superintendent of Central Excise to the effect that ‘E’ Ltd. had not taken credit of duty paid on the said shredded steel scrap, was not doubted by the Excise authorities. Similarly, the certificate issued by another Superintendent to the effect that the quantity of shredded steel scrap received by the appellant from ‘E’ Ltd. had been used as inputs in the factory of the appellant, was also not doubted by the Excise authorities. In these circumstances, the appellant had established that the credit of duty on receipt of imported shredded steel scrap from ‘E’ Ltd. had been taken in accordance with law. [Para 9]

Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Invoice - both Jind and Faridabad mentioned in consignee's address in the invoice - credit not to be denied as respondents have produced evidence of movement and receipt of input into the factory - appeal dismissed (Para 3)

HEADNOTE: Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Procedure to be observed by manufacturer - Whether gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994, but endorsed after that date, would fall under coverage of Entry No. 10 in Table to Notification No. 16/94-CE (NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently be eligible documents for taking credit under Modvat Scheme - Held, yes [Para 3] Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994, Circular No. 600/37/2001-CX, dated 19-11-2001

FACT: The Tribunal held that the gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994, but endorsed after that date, would fall under the coverage of Entry No. 10 in the Table to the Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently, be eligible documents for taking credit under the Modvat Scheme. It rejected the objection of the revenue that the endorsement should also have been made on the gate-passes on or before 1-4-1994, by observing that endorsed gate-pass was not comparable to the issue of gate-pass because what is mentioned in the proviso to the Notification is that documents should have been issued, which meant that gate-passes should have been issued on or before 1-4-1994.

On reference :

HELD: As per the position prevailing prior to 30-3-1994, when the purchaser resold inputs to third party, he would make an endorsement on the gate pass issued by the manufacturer of the input. Procedure had changed and instead of endorsement on the gate-passes, invoice was required to be produced as per Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994. Certain documents were prescribed for the purpose of giving credit of Modvat under the Rules. In Column No. 3 to the Entry No. 10 of the aforesaid Notification, prescribed documents were endorsed gate-passes/subsidiary gate-passes/certificates. Admittedly, gate-passes were required to be issued by the manufacturer under the procedure then prevailing and as and when the purchaser of the inputs resold inputs to third party, he would make an endorsement on the gate-pass, which would authorise the purchaser to take benefit of the credit of the duties paid on the goods. From the language of the said Notification, it is clear that benefit could be given if the documents would have been issued before 1-4-1994 and credit had been taken on or before 30-6-1994. From this, it was clear that gate-passes could be issued before 1-4-1994 and the benefit of credit could be taken on or before 30-6-1994. Transaction of sale or re-sale could take place any time prior to 30th June and on endorsement of same being made, benefit could be taken on or before 30-6-1994. The language of the Notification nowhere requires that the endorsement should also be made before 1-4-1994. [Para 1]

Therefore, gate-passes issued prior to 1-4-1994 but endorsed after that date would fall under the coverage of Entry No. 10 in the Table to the Notification No. 16/94-CE(NT), dated 30-3-1994 and would, consequently, be eligible documents for taking credit under the Modvat Scheme. [Para 3]

HEADNOTE: Rule 9, read with Rules 2(a), 3 and 4 of the Cenvat Credit Rules, 2004, Rule 4A and Rule 4B of the Service Tax Rules, 1994 and Rule 11 of the Central Excise Rules, 2002 - Cenvat Credit - Documents on which credit may be taken - Assessee was manufacturing dutiable products under lease agreement with DSM - DSM had provided capital goods to assessee and said capital goods were installed and used by assessee - Assessee took credit of duty paid on capital goods on basis of supplier's invoice, which was in name of DSM and was endorsed by DSM to effect that 'goods covered under these invoices are transferred to assessee in view of lease agreement' - Department denied credit on ground that Endorsed invoices which are in name of DSM Sugars cannot be held to be proper Cenvatable document - HELD : Since there was no dispute that said capital goods were : (a) received by assessee, (b) duly installed in their factory and (c) used for manufacture of final product cleared by assessee, revenue's objection that such CENVAT credit is not available on basis of endorsed invoices cannot be upheld - Since this was not a case of 'sale' by one manufacturer to another and was a case of lessor buying and supplying capital goods to assessee-lessee's factory, certificate by lessor DSM as endorsement on invoice would be sufficient to take credit [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]Cenvat Credit : Where lessee is manufacturing goods under lease agreement with lessor and lessor supplies capital goods to lessee, lessee may take credit on basis of supplier's invoice in name of lessor but endorsed by lessor in favour of lesse.

FACT: Facts

The assessee is engaged in the manufacture of mould steel ingots and runners and risers under an agreement entered into by them with DSM Sugar Asmoli.

Under the said lease agreement dated 26-09-2002, the facility of land and machinery stands provided by DSM Sugar, Asmoli and the capital goods were received by them are required to be installed by the assessee and the duty on the final product required to be paid by the assessee.

DSM Sugars, Asmoli had endorsed the said invoices indicating as "certified that the goods covered under these invoices transferred to Kailash Steel, Asmoli in view of lease agreement dated 20-09-2002".

The Department denied CENVAT credit to the assessee on the ground that the invoices issued by the supplier are in the name of DSM Sugars, Asmoli, though there is no dispute that the said capital goods were received by the assessee and were duly erected and installed in their premises and were used for the manufacture of dutiable and excisable goods.

Revenue's Arguments

Endorsed invoices which are in the name of DSM Sugars cannot be held to be proper Cenvatable document so as to allow the CENVAT credit in respect of the same, to the assessee.

Assessee's Arguments

Even though DSM Sugars are the owners of the capital goods in question, there is no sale purchase of the capital goods and the same only stands transferred to their unit under the lease agreement, in which case, the effect of endorsement would not be of much relevance.

HELD: In as much as there is no dispute that the said capital goods stand received by the assessees and further duly installed in their factory and were being used for the manufacture of the final product, which was being cleared by the assessee, the revenue's objection that such CENVAT credit is not available in as much as the same was taken on the basis of the endorsed invoices cannot be upheld.

Admittedly, this is not a case of sale of capital goods from one manufacturer unit to another. It is a case where the capital goods are bought by the lessor and transferred to the lessee's factory, under lease agreement for further manufacture of the final product. As such, the certificate given by DSM Sugars, Asmoli on the invoices indicating that are being transferred and in the absence of any dispute to the factual aspect, the assessee is entitled to the CENVAT credit involved in the present appeal. [Para 4]

11. In CCE&C v. Steelco Gujarat Ltd. 2010 (255) ELT 518 (Guj.), the original/duplicate invoices had been lost in transit. As such, the assessee availed CENVAT credit on the basis of xerox copy of the triplicate copy of the invoice, duly attested by the Jurisdictional Range Superintendent at the suppliers end to evidence the duty payment character of the said invoice in question.

The Commissioner of Central Excise (Appeals) observed that there was no dispute about the duty paid character of the input, receipt of the same in the appellant’s factory and utilization for manufacture of final product. Therefore, the Commissioner of Central Excise (Appeals) came to the conclusion that the legitimate right of the appellants cannot be denied just because the original/duplicate invoices were lost in transit. The department could at best, as a precaution to prevent availment of double credit in the case of appellants recover the original document and insist for an undertaking or indemnity bond from the appellants.

The Tribunal while confirming the order of the Commissioner of Central Excise (Appeals) observed that mere xerox copy by itself should not be made the basis of allowing the credit but where the assessee had made efforts to get the said xerox copy attested by the Range Superintendent at the supplier’s end and had established beyond doubt that the duty, stood paid on the goods and the goods stood received by him, denial of credit on the procedural irregularity would not be justified.

The High Court did not find any infirmity in the order passed by the Tribunal and Commissioner of Central Excise (Appeals).

The appellants also relied upon the decision of the Tribunal in the case of Chrome Chemical Industries vs. Commissioner of Central Excise, Calcutta-IV, reported in 2001 (135) ELT 405 (Tri.-Kolkata), wherein in similar situation the credit was allowed.

4. In respect of the credit where the address of the Firm was not mentioned, the contention of the appellant is that in the month of April, 1998 they closed their manufacturing Unit at Mathura Road and started a fresh Unit at Village Bhagola, Palwal and after getting a fresh registration. The manufacturer were continued to mention their old address on the invoices. Appellants relied upon the decision of the Larger Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Kamakhya Steels (P) Ltd. vs.Commissioner of Central Excise, Meerut reported in 2000 (40) RLT 575 (CEGAT-LB)=RLT (L.B.-CEGAT)-1907=2000 (121) ELT 247 (Tribunal-LB) where the Tribunal considered the amendment to the Rule 57G and 57T.

5. The learned Departmental Representative appeared on behalf of the Revenue reiterated the finding of the lower authority submitted the invoices should be in the name of the manufacturing Unit and by mentioning wrong address of the Unit, appellants are not entitled for the credit.

6. I find that the Central Board of Excise and Customs issued a Circular dated 14.5.1996, to remove the difficulties where the invoices were in the name of the Head Office and the credit was taken in the manufacturing Unit. The Tribunal in the case of Chrome Chemical Industries vs. Commissioner of Central Excise (Calcutta-IV (Supra) after considering this Circular held that manufacturing Unit is entitled for credit where the invoices were in the name of Registered office in case the invoices were not endorsed by the Head office which is only a procedural lapse. In these circumstances the credit cannot be denied to the appellants on the ground that the invoices were in the name of the Head office.

7. The factory premises of the appellants were shifted to a new place in the month of April, 1998 but they were receiving invoices on the old address. The Tribunal in the case of Kamakhya Steels (P) Ltd. after taking into consideration the amendment to Rule 57G and 57T of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 by Notification No. 7/99-CE(NT) dated 9.2.1999 held that the credit shall be denied on the ground that any of the documents, mentioned in Sub-Rule (3) does not contain all the particulars required to be contained under these rules, if such document contains details of payment of duty, description of the goods, assessable value, name and address of the factory.

8. In the present case admittedly the factory premises were shifted to the new place whereas on the invoice the old address was mentioned where no manufacturing activities were carried out. In these circumstances, the appellants are entitled for the credit of these invoices also. The impugned order is set aside and the appeals are allowed.

FACT: The assessee was engaged in the manufacture of polyester filament yarn. It availed credit of service tax during the period from October, 2005 to March, 2006 on the basis of invoices which were not in the name of its factory. In the impugned order, the Commissioner (Appeals) had held that it was only a procedural omission and therefore, the credit taken by the assessee was in order. On that ground as well as on the ground of limitation, he had dropped the demand and also set aside the penalty but had imposed a penalty of Rs. 10,000 under rule 15(1).

On cross-appeals :

HELD: The Commissioner (Appeals) had rightly followed the decision of the Tribunal in the case of CCE&CE v. DNH Spinners [2010] 25 STT 295 (Ahd. - CESTAT). Even though the assessee had multiple divisions, in the absence of any dispute about the receipt of the services in question by the factory to whom credit had been passed on, the ratio of the cited decision was applicable. In fact, the Commissioner(Appeals) proceeded to say that the assessee should have followed the procedure of issue of invoices by the head office as an input service distributor but observed that as far as the present appeal was concerned, the proceedings were limited by the ground taken in the show-cause notice and the order-in-original which had held that assessee had taken credit wrongly since invoice was not in its name but in the name of its head office. In view of the fact that the invoice was in the name of the head office and there was no dispute raised in the show-cause notice as to the admissibility of input service credit to the factory on the ground that the input service was not relatable to the factory, the omission became a totally curable defect and was a condonable one. Under those circumstances, the conclusion reached by the Commissioner (Appeals) to drop the demand could not be found fault with. The Commissioner (Appeals) also had taken a view that merely because the assessee did not disclose to the department that it had availed credit on the basis of documents not prescribed under rule 9(2), it could not be said that there was suppression of fact, wilful misstatement, etc. He had relied upon the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Larsen & Toubro Ltd. v. CCE 2007 (211) ELT 513. In view of the fact that there was no allegation of non-receipt of input service or the allegation of service not relatable to the factory and also in view of the fact that invoice was in the name of head office of the same factory and not in the name of someone else, the decision of the Commissioner (Appeals) that extended period was not invocable also had to be upheld. Since the assessee was eligible for the credit and there was no suppression of facts, extended period was not invocable and, hence, the question of penalty did not arise. Accordingly, the penalty imposed was to be set aside. In view of the above, the appeal filed by the revenue was to be rejected and appeal filed by the assessee was to be allowed. [Para 2]
